# `main` is RED on the comment-hygiene gate: three rot-prone run-id references

## Symptom

`python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` fails on current `gerrit/main`:

    comment-hygiene: 3 rot-prone reference(s) found
      tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:56  [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:1         [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:152       [run-id]  30836378745

The gate runs in the `lint + type-check` job, which is one of the six gating jobs behind the
`Verified` vote. **So every change pushed for review right now inherits a `Verified -1` it did not
cause.** Observed on Gerrit change 1311, whose own (unrelated) hygiene violations were fixed and
which still failed on these three.

## Cause

The references landed with story f124 (`9af278b01f` "live external suite covers many providers" and
`1d75850974` "close the ambient-default provider leak"), which cite CI run `30836378745` in
docstrings as the evidence for why each test exists.

They were presumably clean when written; the gate itself is recent (`f2b2d0b410` added it, and
`d4095763e3` "Fix comment-hygiene acceptor path false-accept" TIGHTENED it). A gate that gets
stricter after content lands will surface exactly this shape — pre-existing prose that was
acceptable under the looser rule.

## Why the content is worth keeping, and what to do instead

These are not padding. Each docstring explains that the test exists **because a real leak shipped**,
and the run id is the evidence. The gate's own message names the accepted alternatives: cite a
resolvable ticket id, drop the token for durable prose, or mark it `context: external`.

Story f124 is the durable home for the run id. The fix is to keep the reasoning and cite f124 rather
than the run number — the same edit ticket 39c1's cells took.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` exits 0 on `main`
- [x] the three docstrings KEEP their explanation of why each test exists — this is a citation
      change, not a deletion; a fix that removes the reasoning is a regression in a different
      direction
- [x] the run id is replaced by a reference a reader can still resolve (the f124 ticket)
- [x] no test behaviour changes: the suites that cover these files pass unchanged

## Note on ordering

Worth landing AHEAD of other in-flight changes, since it unblocks the `Verified` vote for everything
currently in review.
